recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No current FHIR core source change is recommended unless a human is maintaining a historical DSTU2 branch or identifies a distinct ServiceRequest ordering problem under a new tracker.
issue_request: FHIR-12689 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU2 Patient Care QA issue reporting that ReferralRequest elements were out of order, specifically that serviceRequested belonged near the requested service portion of the resource rather than last and that authored/fulfillmentTime ordering should match the QA expectation.
initial_application: Git commit e73353ab39a4227a35c7ec0fe8d20c75161c7064 explicitly named #12689 and edited the then-active source/referralrequest spreadsheet files, including moving ReferralRequest.serviceRequested from the last row to before ReferralRequest.patient. Concurrent #10293 workflow-alignment edits changed related request-workflow rows, including authored/authoredOn handling.
additional_context: FHIR-13196 later approved merging ReferralRequest and ProcedureRequest into ServiceRequest because the resource boundary was unclear. Current source/fhir.ini actively registers servicerequest=ServiceRequest, records that ReferralRequest became ServiceRequest, and retains only historical ReferralRequest rename mappings. The current source tree has no active ReferralRequest StructureDefinition.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Editing retired ReferralRequest source would be out of current build scope, and the active ServiceRequest definition has a different post-merge element sequence rather than the DSTU2 ReferralRequest ordering defect.

related_jiras.note: Published follow-up that merged ReferralRequest and ProcedureRequest into ServiceRequest, explaining why the FHIR-12689 target resource is retired in the current build.
